name: asking to clarify context
def: Tutor asks the student about the problem to understand the context or asks for clarification about what the student said about the problem

ex.q: Do you have to just state whether it's positive or negative or exact slopes?

name: probing prior knowledge
def: Tutor probes about student's prior knowledge. It should be a yes or no question.

ex.q: Did you learn about this?
Are you familiar with area and perimeter in any way?

name: probing understanding
def: Tutor questions whether student understood the statement made or step(s) done. It should be a yes or no question.

ex.q: Do you get that?
Are you with me?
Does that make sense?
Do you know why I did that?

name: correcting own error
def: Tutor explicitly recognizes a mathematical error they made.

ex.q: My bad actually you're right, we don't need that distance, we just need the height

name: strategizing
def: Tutor situates the session, including discussing learning goals and the plan to complete the problem.

ex.q: I think the approach here might be to write multiple equations of what we know, and to then create a system of equations to solve these together
so what we found out is that our equation, as we move to the right, grows without limit
Okay, so we're going to estimate the position of tens and hundreds on a number line.

name: prompting related knowledge
def: Tutor prompts the student to make connections to related knowledge without giving detailed explanations of the related knowledge.

ex.q: okay first explain what that regression line is i need to make sure you know it
So, what can you tell me about the place value chart? What happens in it usually?

name: prompting related representation
def: Tutor asks the student to represent the idea in a different form.

ex.q: can you write that as an question
draw that on the graph
shall we try it using the place value chart as well?

name: prompting explanation
def: Tutor prompts the student to explain actions or knowledge.

ex.q: Why did you do that?
What is this?
What did you do?
How did you get?
So what do you know about what is shown so far?
Please show your work
Yeah. So, if we look at hundreds, tens and ones, can you tell me the relationship between those three?

name: prompting action
def: Tutor prompts the student to produce any problem-solving step without adding new information.

ex.q: what'd you get?
Can you do the first step
Do you remember?
Could you try to solve it first? Please tell me when you get stuck. What are you going to do next?
Asking the student to read the question.

name: prompting correction
def: Tutor prompts the student to correct their own mistakes without giving away the right way.

ex.q: can you recheck the first and third, middle one's right

name: feedback correct
def: Tutor indicates that the student has provided a correct response.

ex.q: That's right
Second blue one looks good!

name: feedback incorrect
def: Tutor indicates that the student has provided an incorrect response.

ex.q: Hmm close
not exactly

name: feedback neutral
def: Tutor comments without confirming accuracy or inaccuracy.

ex.q: Don't worry about finding the actual number
yes in a sense

name: revoicing
def: Tutor says what the student said in different ways.

ex.q: You stated earlier that we must add the like terms?

name: restating
def: Tutor says what the student said verbatim.

lines.say: Well, I basically just got rid of the zero on the end.
Got rid of the zero. Okay. So, can you do the same from over here? Can you do the same in this question?

name: giving hint
def: Tutor provides a suggestion to guide the student toward a solution without revealing the answer.

ex.q: maybe use the line to help you fine the slop
you can do that, but there might be a slightly easier way

name: giving example
def: Tutor uses an example that is different from the student's problem.

ex.q: Ok lets say instead of the diameter being 3 its 1

name: explaining conceptual
def: Tutor gives instruction on general concepts or facts.

ex.q: It's because between the two roots (one positive and one negative) - the slope has to change from positive to negative and to do that there as to be a turning point whcih is a local max or min

name: explaining procedural
def: Tutor gives instructions about the context of the question and algorithmic process to solve the problem.

ex.q: substitute 1 in for r and 1 in for H
we are supposed to make an equation that states how many people are unable to read after t years

name: giving answer
def: Tutor provides a solution without including the solution steps.

ex.q: In this case it would be 10.5/14

name: building rapport
def: Tutor engages in relationship building conversation, including when the tutor humanizes themselves.

ex.q: excuse my poor drawings

name: encouraging
def: Tutor makes encouraging statements to students.

ex.q: Good question
Take ur time!
Um, just seem to be missing something. And I think you know what it is.

name: asking feeling
def: Tutor asks for the student's feelings.

ex.q: Hi, how's it going?

name: validating feeling
def: Tutor validates the student's feelings.

ex.q: Fair point

name: praising process
def: Tutor praises the student's process of solving the problem.

ex.q: Great job!
Keep up the great work.

name: praising outcome
def: Tutor praises the student's outcome of student work.

ex.q: Great job on your success!
Great work getting an A!
which you've been acing on the past two questions

name: praising trait
def: Tutor praises the student's characteristic.

ex.q: You are so smart!

name: technical issues
def: Tutor makes a comment related to technical problems of the tutoring context.

ex.q: I don't see anything on the whiteboard. Did you use a text box?
Nice, I can see it
Sure send a chat when u finsh.

name: managing
def: Tutor announces rules, manages time, schedules next sessions, etc.

ex.q: we prefer students to solve on board so that we can check their solutions for any errors
okay but i will not be allowed to totally answer them for you just assist you okay?
